g1.label: 1. Spend billions to ___ us
g1.why: The text says companies want to persuade us to buy their products, not forget or ignore us.

g2.label: 2. Grabs your ___
g2.why: The text says a good advert grabs your attention immediately.

g3.label: 3. A catchy ___
g3.why: ‘Catchy slogan’ is the fixed phrase describing a memorable advertising line.

g4.label: 4. Famous people, or ___
g4.why: The text says adverts use famous people, i.e. celebrities, whose products we trust.

g5.label: 5. Special ___
g5.why: ‘Special offers’ (like buy one get one free) is the fixed advertising phrase.

g6.label: 6. "Brand ___"
g6.why: ‘Brand new’ is the fixed advertising phrase, not ‘brand old’ or ‘brand broken’.

g7.label: 7. "Limited ___"
g7.why: ‘Limited edition’ is the fixed advertising phrase making a product sound rare.

g8.label: 8. We ___ something we never wanted
g8.why: The text says adverts make us feel we need things, not hate or lose them.

g1.label: 1. "___ our brand new range!"
g1.why: Adverts use the imperative (command) form, so the base verb ‘Discover’ is used.

g2.label: 2. "The ___ pizza in town!"
g2.why: ‘The’ + superlative ‘best’ makes the strongest claim, not the comparative ‘better’.

g3.label: 3. "Don't ___ this deal!"
g3.why: Negative imperatives use ‘Don’t’ + the base verb: ‘Don’t miss’.

g4.label: 4. "___ it now!"
g4.why: Adverts use the imperative (command) form, so the base verb ‘Try’ is used.

g5.label: 5. "An ___ new taste!"
g5.why: An adjective is needed before the noun, so the -ing adjective ‘amazing’ is used, not the verb ‘amaze’.

g6.label: 6. "This is a ___ offer!"
g6.why: ‘Limited offer’ is the fixed phrase for a short-time deal.

g7.label: 7. "Buy one, get one ___!"
g7.why: ‘Buy one, get one free’ is the fixed phrase for this kind of offer.

g8.label: 8. "Introducing our ___ design!"
g8.why: Adverts promote new products, so ‘new’ fits the promotional tone, not ‘old’ or ‘broken’.
